ruleset.name: JustSearch PMD Ruleset — Java test sources
ruleset.description:
Ruleset for every Java source set that is not `main` — `test`, `integrationTest`, `systemTest`, `determinismTest`, `testFixtures`. (`soakTest` was in this list until lane F stage A item A12 removed the only source set that had one.) Applied by `JvmBaseConventionsPlugin` to every `Pmd` task except `pmdMain` (tempdoc 930 §22.2 follow-up 10, which put those tasks in `check`/`build`).
It is `ruleset.xml` minus exactly two rules, each dropped because its PREMISE — not merely its noise level — is false in a test source set. Both counts were measured on the 569 pre-existing violations cleared by that change:
SystemPrintln (127 violations). The rule exists so that shipped output is routable and level-filterable through SLF4J. A test's console output IS its report: it is read by whoever ran the suite, from the Gradle/CI log, and there is no operator to reconfigure. Same reasoning as `ruleset-cli-tools.xml` applies to CLI entry points.
NonThreadSafeSingleton (17 violations). The rule detects racing lazy initialisation of a static field. All 17 were `@BeforeAll`/`@AfterAll` fixture setup and teardown of the shape `if (worker != null) { worker.close(); worker = null; }`. JUnit runs lifecycle callbacks once, serialised by the framework, so no race is expressible there.
Everything else in `ruleset.xml` is kept, deliberately: `CommentContent` (a parked marker in a test is the same deferred fix as one in main), the whole `Unused*` family (dead test code is the easiest kind to accumulate), `UnnecessaryFullyQualifiedName`, and `EmptyCatchBlock` — whose `allowCommentedBlocks` / `allowExceptionNameRegex` properties already exempt a documented empty catch and an `expected`-named one, which is every legitimate case a test has.
KEEP IN SYNC with `ruleset.xml` — rules are inlined rather than referenced because PMD's `rule ref` resolves against the classpath, not the working directory; a file-path ref fails with "Cannot resolve rule/ruleset reference" and PMD then analyses NOTHING while Gradle still reports success (probed 2026-09-05). `scripts/ci/check-pmd-ruleset-sync.mjs` enforces the sync so that silent-dormancy mode cannot be reached by drift.
